title: No first-class Rust crate-extraction facility (monolith → workspace-member crate)
wanted_capability:
A reusable way to extract a cohesive subsystem out of a monolithic crate into a new workspace-member crate, as a guarded/transactional operation. Concretely: (1) scaffold the new crate — create crates/<name>/Cargo.toml ([package] + inferred [dependencies]) and src/lib.rs, add <name> to the root [workspace].members, and add <name> = { path = "crates/<name>" } to each named consumer's [dependencies]; (2) move the chosen modules/items into it with visibility bumped to pub at the new crate boundary; (3) crate-aware path rewrite — rewrite `crate::<seg>` / `use crate::<seg>` references in the origin crate to `<new_crate>::<seg>` (with use-tree splitting), and rewrite references from the extracted code back into the origin to `<origin_crate>::...`; (4) DAG guard — verify the extraction keeps the workspace dependency graph acyclic (this repo's contract-bottom invariant: implementation crates point down, never sideways/up); (5) validate via cargo check --workspace + rust_compile_fix_round with rollback across all writes. Ideal shape is a compound bbox_refactor_run macro `extract_rust_crate`, directly analogous to the existing `migrate_rust_mods_to_lib` macro but one level out (package→new-package instead of bin→lib), optionally fronted by a refactor atom for autonomous repeat use.</wanted_capability>
<parameter name="missing_primitive">A `extract_rust_crate` compound plan/macro (bbox_refactor_run) plus its three missing sub-primitives: a workspace-crate scaffolder (Cargo.toml + lib.rs + members + consumer dep-edge wiring), a crate-aware path rewriter (`crate::`/`use crate::` ↔ `<crate>::` with use-tree splitting, generalizing rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths beyond the bin→lib case), and a workspace-DAG acyclicity check.</missing_primitive>
<parameter name="fallback_used">Hand-compose the sequence from existing within-crate primitives: write_file + multiple ensure_toml_table for scaffolding and dep wiring; rust_top_level_dependency_analysis to find the seam; extract_rust_items_to_submodule / move_rust_items_with_local_deps to move the cluster; migrate_rust_mods_to_lib / rewrite_rust_bin_crate_paths / move_rust_items_with_callers approximate the path rewrite (simple-name-segment match only, not crate-path aware, no use-tree splitting — leftovers need manual cleanup); rewrite_rust_*_visibility for the pub bump; bbox_refactor_run with cargo gates + rust_compile_fix_round to converge. No DAG cycle guard exists; relies on cargo check failing.</fallback_used>

notes:
Motivated by the ~15m (now ~4m) release build: the 277k-LOC root `blackbox` crate is the serial-frontend pole, so peeling cold subsystems into their own crates is a recurring, ongoing need. extract_rust_crate = the migrate_rust_mods_to_lib transactional shape (scaffold -> move -> rewrite crate:: paths -> check -> fix-round -> final check) generalized to arbitrary crate boundaries, plus a scaffolder, a crate-aware path rewriter, and a workspace-DAG acyclicity guard (the harness<->daemon boundary is compiler-enforced acyclic; a cycle-introducing extraction would violate it silently until link time).

CAMPAIGN OF RECORD — code-intelligence cluster split (chunker -> lsp -> refactor -> code_nav-syntax -> macros, ~114k LOC, on a bbox-corpus-core foundation). Staging: [0] bbox-corpus-core {entity_ref,git[+util,json_store,projects,edit-DTOs later]}; [1] bbox-chunker; [2] bbox-lsp; [3] bbox-refactor (the 91k prize); [4] bbox-code-nav (split: syntax-nav moves, code_symbols_indexed + MCP adapter + the index dep stay root-side; inline the 3 tantivy helpers); [5] bbox-macros. Key facts (4-bro fan-out): refactor->tools is test-only (leave in root); lsp->refactor is REAL (lsp/convert.rs imports FileEdit/TextEdit/path_string/sha256_hex — lower those 4 DTOs to foundation to break the cycle, then lsp sits below refactor); macros' 6 code_nav symbols are all index-free (macros does NOT drag index in); index is woven into SharedState/startup (stays root). STATUS: stages 0-1 DONE + committed (3b6b31f1), validated green. Next: stage 2 (bbox-lsp) + the edit-DTO lowering.

FINDINGS the facility must automate (accumulated across all 3 worked extractions):

1. DEP ENUMERATION must scan (a) inline-qualified `<crate>::` paths not just `use` lines [vectors: missed dirs/tempfile], (b) test-only deps -> [dev-dependencies] [vectors: tempfile], AND (c) **self-references by the crate's OWN PACKAGE NAME** [corpus-core: git.rs called `blackbox::config::load()` — invisible to a `crate::`-pattern scan, made git look like a leaf when it secretly reached UP into config]. A `crate::`-only coupling scan UNDER-counts upward edges; must also grep `<own_package_name>::`.

2. UPWARD-EDGE INVERSION: when a would-be-foundation module reaches up into the root (config/state/etc.), invert it via a startup-injected OnceLock instead of moving the whole upper module down. Pattern: child exposes `set_X()` (pub), root calls it once after the relevant load; child falls back to env/default absent injection (behavior-preserving). [corpus-core git notes namespace <- blackbox::config, fixed via git::set_notes_namespace called from server/open.rs].

3. cfg(test) ITEMS CONSUMED ACROSS THE BOUNDARY need a `test-support` feature gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature=\"test-support\"))]` on defs AND read-paths, enabled via a parent dev-dependency. [vectors needed it; corpus-core + chunker did NOT — detect per-extraction, don't assume].

4. LOW-COLLISION CALLER REWRITE: re-export alias `use <child> as <oldmod>;` (or `pub use` to preserve a pub module) in the parent lib.rs makes all `crate::<oldmod>::*` resolve unchanged — DEFAULT strategy, especially on hot shared branches (0 churn across 25 git + 23 chunker + 9 vectors inbound sites). Private `use child as m;` at crate root is crate-wide visible (root's descendants), matching the original private `mod m;`.

5. SELECTIVE pub PROMOTION: pub(crate) items reached across the boundary must become pub. Wholesale `pub(crate)->pub` in the moved file is acceptable for internal foundation crates (over-exposure harmless, saves churn vs per-symbol); but same-named methods/items used only internally could stay pub(crate) if a tighter surface is wanted.

6. SELF-PATH REWRITE: absolute `crate::<oldmod>::sub::` self-references inside the moved code become `crate::sub::` once it IS the crate root. [vectors: crate::vectors::wal:: -> crate::wal::; chunker/corpus-core had none].
